summary: This is a test suite written in Bats (Bash Automated Testing System) that verifies custom assertion functions. It sets up a temporary file before each test and tears it down afterward, then runs tests for binary existence checks and Docker image existence checks, including tests that use mock functions to simulate different scenarios.

explanations.4: bats_load_library loads reusable assertion helpers from the bats-assert library, giving us functions like assert_success and assert_failure that check if commands succeeded or failed.
explanations.7: This sources (includes) a custom assertion script file from your project so the test can call the custom functions being tested, like assert::binaryExists.
explanations.11: This creates the /tmp/bats directory only if it doesn't already exist — the [[ ! -d ... ]] checks if the directory is missing, and && means 'only run the next command if the previous one succeeded'.
explanations.18: The [[ -f ... ]] checks if the temporary file actually exists before trying to delete it, preventing errors if the file was never created.
explanations.24: The run command executes the assert::binaryExists function and captures its exit code and output so the following assertions can check them.
explanations.27: assert_success verifies that the previous command (the one run with 'run') exited with code 0, meaning it succeeded.
explanations.35: assert_output with empty quotes checks that the command produced no output — this is testing that success cases don't print anything.
explanations.43: assert_failure 1 checks that the command failed with exit code 1, indicating an error occurred as expected.
explanations.46: assert_output with a string checks that the command's output exactly matches this error message.
explanations.54: Defining docker() as a function here temporarily overrides the real docker command for this test only, letting us control what it returns without needing actual Docker installed.
explanations.74: assert_output --partial checks that the output contains this text somewhere within it, rather than matching the exact full output.
